literature_notes: All three ledger clips (L1, L2 from PMC8055269; L3 from PMC8989947) describe full-length DCST2 constructs carrying a PA-tag (L1, L2) or a 3xHA-tag (L3), expressed in mouse sperm under the Calmegin promoter for transgenic complementation experiments. The tagged constructs were functional — they restored fertility in Dcst2-null males — confirming the tag does not abolish protein function. However, none of the clips name a residue, a loop, or any positional landmark for where the tag was inserted into the protein sequence. The topology_derived rule (which allows a position to be inferred from landmarks when no residue is named) requires that exactly ONE terminus be extracellular; DCST2 has zero extracellular termini: the N-terminus (residues 1–25) is intracellular and the C-terminus (residues 517–773) is intracellular. No loop is named in any clip, so a region-level site with a null insert_after_residue cannot be created either. Choosing a position inside one of the three extracellular spans (47–51, 114–325, 433–500) on structural or topological grounds alone is explicitly forbidden by the rules. Accordingly, zero sites qualify.
